name: Megyn Kelly
role: American journalist and podcaster (Fox News 2004–2017, NBC 2017–2019, The Megyn Kelly Show 2020–present)
summary: Megyn Kelly describes herself as a registered independent and right-leaning conservative; she supported Trump in 2024. On her own show she opposes illegal immigration and ending protections like TPS, supports capital punishment in the worst cases, rejects gender-identity recognition and trans inclusion in women's sport, opposes new gun control, and favours leaving abortion to the states. Her views on Israel, Iran and Ukraine moved toward a restraint-minded stance after 2025, criticising the 2026 Iran war.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Said the US was built on its 'work ethic and culture and values', that TPS migrants dilute it and that 'more than half of you won't assimilate'.

death-penalty.rationale: Said in December 2025 she wants the death penalty for Tyler Robinson and anyone who helped him and that deterrence 'requires the death penalty in the most heinous of cases', while saying it should be reserved for those.

decide-locally.rationale: Argued in 2022 and 2024 that abortion should be settled state by state in a federalist system, not by nine unelected judges or Congress.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: After the 2023 affirmative action ruling said she 'totally agree[d]' that placing students in schools above their qualifications sets them up to fail, citing her own case of not belonging at Harvard.

exclude-trans-women-women-only-spaces.rationale: In 2023 she said trans women should not use women's locker rooms or bathrooms and that women's spaces must rest on biological sex.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: In 2026 she said Trump's promise of no more Middle East wars was fundamental to her vote and that launching the Iran war was a betrayal; this concerns the Middle East only, and she backed other interventions such as the Caribbean boat strikes.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: In 2023 said she would no longer use preferred pronouns, that a man cannot become a woman, and that trans women should not use women's locker rooms, bathrooms or sports; supports separate or open categories. Noted that workplace anti-discrimination law already covers trans people, without disputing it.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Describes the claim that gender is a social construct as part of a 'fiction' she once went along with and now rejects; insists on biological reality.

limit-guns.rationale: Says she is 'not some huge Second Amendment person' but argues nothing proposed by gun-control advocates will work, bans like the assault weapons ban failed, and calls for shaming 'gun control zealots'; favours mental-health and soft-target remedies instead.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Argues women's rights, spaces and sports must be built on the biological category of women and that including trans women is a 'lie'.

open-borders.rationale: Backs deporting everyone in the country illegally, turning away asylum seekers at the border and ending TPS; opposed Biden-era open-border policy.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Argued that Americans built the country with their work ethic, culture and values and that new arrivals dilute it (June 2026).

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: In March 2022 said a $15 federal minimum wage hurts working people more than it helps because it costs jobs.

reduce-immigration.rationale: In June 2026 she welcomed the Supreme Court rulings on asylum and ending TPS for Haitians and Syrians ('Go home. Get out.'), and in January 2026 said the mandate Trump was elected on was to rid the country of all illegal immigrants.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In 2013 said Tony Perkins' arguments against same-sex marriage were not persuasive and that its advocates had made a credible case; in 2022 noted gay marriage has majority support and she did not oppose it. Never stated her own support directly.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Insists that sex is biological reality ('a man can't become a woman') and objects to the idea that sex is a social category.

student-debt-relief.rationale: In 2022 said she did not think a neighbour should have to pay for her or others' college education and opposed cancelling student debt (quoted in a reaction video playing her clip).

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: In April 2026 objected to California's proposed 5 percent billionaire wealth tax, saying the money was already earned and taxed.

turn-back-illegal-migrants.rationale: In June 2026 she welcomed rulings letting the government turn away asylum seekers at the border and backs deporting everyone in the country illegally.

notes: Only Kelly's own statements were used; questions she asked guests and guests' views were excluded. As a Fox anchor (2013-2017) she mostly acted as a news presenter, so those years yield little of her own opinion. No evidence found that she has taken a political quiz on camera. Abortion: she has argued the Dobbs ruling was legally right and that abortion is a states' issue, but has not clearly stated her own view on legality, so it is left null. Israel: she calls herself on Israel's side and said Israel was right to respond to October 7, but by August 2025 argued Israel was losing the propaganda war and should wrap up the Gaza war; these did not match a statement closely enough to answer. Ukraine: she backs Trump's settlement push and criticises Zelensky, with no matching statement answered. COVID: pro-vaccine for adults, doubts the legality of the 2021 OSHA mandate and calls school policies 'insanity', but no statement fits. Islam: her earlier rhetoric was stronger; in May 2026 she said she is re-evaluating it, so the incompatibility statement is left null. Statement answers are weighted toward 2022-2026. Later pass (2026-11-24): new statements checked against Kelly's own words; YouTube was rate-limited, so only transcripts on Media Matters and National Review were read. Themes searched: gender/children, foreign policy, torture, immigration.
